articles.title: Jio Files for India's Biggest-Ever IPO — and for the First Time, the Diaspora Can Own a Piece of It
articles.excerpt: Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms has filed papers for a Mumbai listing aiming to raise around $3.8 billion, eclipsing every IPO India has seen. For NRIs who use Jio to call home, the company they rely on is about to become one they can invest in.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; Jio Platforms has filed for what would be India’s largest-ever IPO, aiming to raise around $3.8 billion
articles.nri_angle: Jio is the invisible infrastructure of diaspora life — the SIM in a parent's phone, the data behind every video call home, the connection that keeps NRI families tethered to India. Now the company behind it is filing for the country's largest-ever IPO, turning a service the diaspora depends on into an asset it can, for the first time, actually own a share of.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRIs Are Breaking Their Own Bank Deposits to Chase a Better Rate — and Banks Want the RBI's Blessing
articles.excerpt: A new scheme pays NRIs up to 7.1 percent on dollar deposits, but only on fresh money. Those who locked in months ago at half that rate are now paying penalties to break and rebook — and lenders fear $1 billion could walk out the door.
articles.image_caption: US and Indian currency; NRIs are breaking old dollar deposits to rebook at sharply higher rates
articles.nri_angle: This is a pure diaspora money story: it is NRIs who hold these dollar deposits, NRIs being courted by the new higher rates, and NRIs now weighing whether to pay a penalty to break an old deposit and rebook — a decision facing anyone in the community who parked dollars in an Indian bank in the past year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Banks Want to Lend You the Dollars to Deposit With Them — and GIFT City Is the Catch
articles.excerpt: Lenders are pressing the RBI to let their GIFT City branches finance the diaspora dollar-deposit scheme designed to shore up the rupee. Nomura reckons the plan could pull in $55 billion — most of it from NRIs — with the bulk arriving by September.
articles.image_caption: Indian and US currency; banks want to fund the RBI's diaspora dollar-deposit scheme via GIFT City branches
articles.nri_angle: This entire scheme is built around the diaspora's dollars — it is NRIs the RBI is trying to coax into Indian banks to defend the rupee — so the mechanics of how banks fund it, and the leverage being negotiated behind the scenes, directly shape the returns and risks facing any overseas Indian weighing an FCNR deposit this summer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Pulled Back From the Stock Market in May — but Their Monthly SIPs Hit a Record Anyway
articles.excerpt: Equity mutual fund inflows fell 40 percent to a 12-month low as global jitters spooked lump-sum investors, yet automated SIP contributions climbed to an all-time high of ₹26,688 crore — a sign of how deeply disciplined investing has taken root.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee notes; monthly SIP contributions hit a record even as equity fund inflows slumped in May
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who invest in Indian mutual funds through SIPs to stay financially anchored to home, the data is reassuring: India's market is now propped up by steady domestic discipline rather than fickle foreign money, meaning the rupee-cost-averaging strategy many diaspora investors quietly run every month is exactly the behaviour holding the market up.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Five-Day Market Rally Just Snapped — and It Was the IT Giants That Broke It.
articles.excerpt: The Sensex and Nifty slid on Friday as the Nifty IT index crashed to a three-year low, dragged down by an Accenture warning that has put Infosys, Wipro and TCS squarely in investors' crosshairs.
articles.image_caption: An Indian stock-market display; the Sensex and Nifty fell as IT stocks slid to a three-year low
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT is the diaspora's most personal trade — many NRIs work for or hold shares in Infosys, TCS, Wipro and Accenture itself, and a three-year low in the IT index driven by cautious US client spending speaks directly to both their portfolios and their job security in the tech corridors of New Jersey, Texas and the Bay Area.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cheaper Oil Should Be Lifting the Rupee. India's Own Central Bank Is Quietly Holding It Back.
articles.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India's short-dollar forward book has ballooned to a record near $110 billion, and unwinding it — along with hedging the dollars Indian banks are now borrowing abroad — is set to cap the rupee's recovery even as oil sits at three-month lows. For NRIs, it explains why the currency has steadied near 94.5 rather than surged.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee currency; the RBI's record forward book is set to cap the rupee's recovery despite cheaper oil
articles.nri_angle: NRIs watching the rupee to time remittances, deposits and Indian investments need to understand why a clear tailwind — cheap oil — is not translating into a stronger currency: the RBI's record forward-book overhang means dollar inflows are being absorbed to rebuild reserves rather than allowed to lift the rupee.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Banks Are Rushing to Borrow Dollars Abroad — and the RBI Just Made It Cheaper to Do So
articles.excerpt: HDFC Bank, State Bank of India and Bank of Baroda are all tapping the overseas dollar-bond market this month, the first to use a new Reserve Bank facility that subsidises the cost of hedging foreign borrowing. Bankers expect $15–20 billion to flow in over the next six months — a deliberate effort to defend the rupee and pull in foreign capital.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee currency; India's banks are raising dollars overseas under a new RBI subsidised hedging window
articles.nri_angle: NRIs hold a direct stake in the rupee's stability — through remittances, NRE/FCNR deposits and Indian bank shares — and this coordinated push to draw dollars into the banking system is one of the clearest signs of how hard New Delhi is working to steady the currency and fund the economy's growth.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World's Biggest Investors Are Pouring Billions Into India's Data Centres — the Quiet Backbone of the AI Boom
articles.excerpt: Canada's national pension fund just committed $740 million to an Indian data-centre operator, Apple supplier Jabil teamed up with Adani to build AI hardware in the country, and more than $50 billion of digital-infrastructure spending is now in the pipeline. As global capital races to build the physical plumbing of artificial intelligence, India is emerging as a favoured destination — and a fresh theme for NRI investors.
articles.image_caption: Inside a data centre; global investors are pouring billions into India's data-centre capacity to power the AI boom
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs work in the very technology and finance industries driving the global AI build-out, and want exposure to India's growth story beyond real estate and fixed deposits; the data-centre boom — backed by the world's largest pension funds and conglomerates — is becoming one of the most investable expressions of that story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Cleared the Way for Banks to Pay NRIs More on Their Deposits — But Only Until September.
articles.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India has temporarily scrapped the interest-rate ceilings on fresh FCNR(B) and longer-tenure NRE deposits through September 30, freeing banks to compete for overseas money as New Delhi scrambles to defend a battered rupee.
articles.image_caption: Indian currency; the RBI has lifted rate caps on select NRI deposits until September 30 to attract overseas funds
articles.nri_angle: This is one of the most directly actionable moves for NRIs all year: with rate caps lifted on FCNR(B) and long NRE deposits until September 30, banks are about to compete for diaspora dollars — meaning the rates Indians abroad earn on parked savings could jump, but only inside a closing window.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Made It Easier for NRIs to Buy Indian Stocks — RBI Opens a New Repatriable Rupee Account
articles.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India has amended its foreign-exchange rules to let individuals living abroad open dedicated repatriable rupee accounts for investing in listed Indian shares, with sale proceeds free to be sent back overseas. A new 'Individual Foreign Investor' category streamlines the long-tangled plumbing of cross-border equity investment.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India has amended its foreign-exchange rules to ease how individuals abroad invest in listed Indian shares
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs want a stake in India's growth story but have long been deterred by a maze of account types, custodial rules and repatriation friction; this RBI amendment is aimed squarely at them, simplifying how a person abroad can buy Indian shares and — just as importantly — get their money back out.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold's Record Run Has Stalled. After a Blistering Two-Year Rally, the Fed Just Took the Wind Out of It.
articles.excerpt: Bullion that surged 64% in 2025 — its best year in nearly five decades — has slid back below $4,400 an ounce, sinking to a seven-month low this month as a US-Iran peace deal, falling oil and a Federal Reserve hinting at rate hikes drain the fear that powered the climb. In India, prices have eased even as a steep new import duty bites.
articles.image_caption: Gold bullion bars; bullion's record rally has stalled as the Federal Reserve hints at rate hikes
articles.nri_angle: Gold is not merely an asset for the Indian diaspora but a cultural reflex — the default store of value, the wedding gift, the hedge sent home — and after years of one-way gains, the metal's sudden wobble forces NRIs to reckon with whether they are buying a safe haven or chasing a peak that has already passed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Largest Stock Exchange Is Finally Going Public. After a Decade of Delays, the NSE Just Filed Its IPO Papers.
articles.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange — the world's busiest derivatives platform — has filed draft papers for a pure offer-for-sale of up to 149 million shares worth roughly $3 billion, ending a listing saga that began in 2016 and handing long-waiting investors a multi-billion-dollar windfall.
articles.image_caption: A stock exchange trading environment; India's NSE has filed draft papers for its long-delayed IPO
articles.nri_angle: The NSE is the exchange where most of India's listed wealth changes hands — the very market NRIs tap through index funds, ETFs and direct holdings — and owning a slice of the bourse itself, alongside a record year of Indian mega-listings, gives the diaspora a rare chance to bet on the plumbing of India's markets rather than any single stock.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An India-US Trade Deal Is Suddenly Close. The US Trade Chief Visits This Month to Seal the First Tranche.
articles.excerpt: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer travels to New Delhi on June 23-24 to put final touches on an interim agreement, with India's commerce minister signaling the first tranche could be done by mid-July. With a US-Iran truce cooling oil and the World Bank lifting its growth forecast, the macro backdrop has rarely looked better.
articles.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who said the first tranche of an India-US trade deal could be concluded by mid-July
articles.nri_angle: An India-US trade pact sits at the center of the diaspora's two worlds — it shapes the export sectors and equities many NRIs invest in, the rupee that governs how far their remittances stretch, and the broader US-India relationship that frames diaspora life in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Defence Production Hits a Record ₹1.78 Lakh Crore — and the Stocks Riding the Boom Just Surged
articles.excerpt: Government data shows India's annual defence output jumped 15.6 percent to an all-time high, with exports leaping 62 percent to nearly ₹38,500 crore and the private sector's share at a record. The Nifty India Defence index rose 3.9 percent as investors bet the 'Make in India' arms push has real momentum.
articles.image_caption: India's defence production hit a record in FY26; the Nifty India Defence index surged 3.9 percent as exports jumped 62 percent
articles.nri_angle: India's defence-manufacturing boom has become one of the most-watched investment themes for NRIs seeking exposure to the country's industrial rise — a story of self-reliance and export ambition that resonates with diaspora investors looking beyond IT and banks for the next structural growth story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Fed Just Stopped Promising Rate Cuts — and Started Hinting at a Hike. Warsh's First Meeting Spooked Wall Street.
articles.excerpt: In Kevin Warsh's debut as Federal Reserve Chair, the central bank held rates at 3.50–3.75% but flipped its dot plot from an implied cut to an implied hike, sending US stocks sliding and the dollar firmer. For NRIs, a hawkish Fed reshapes everything from the rupee to mortgage rates to the calculus on sending money home.
articles.image_caption: The Federal Reserve in Washington; the Fed held rates but flipped its projections toward a hike at Kevin Warsh's first meeting
articles.nri_angle: A hawkish US Fed keeps the dollar strong and US mortgage and savings rates elevated — directly shaping how much NRIs earn on dollar deposits, what they pay on American home loans, and how many rupees their remittances buy back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Markets Just Logged Their Longest Winning Streak in Two Months. The Engine Is Cheaper Oil — and a Fragile Iran Deal.
articles.excerpt: The Nifty 50 closed above 24,000 for the first time in weeks as benchmarks rose for a fourth straight session, riding a near-three-month low in crude after a US-Iran peace deal promised to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. For NRIs, falling oil is rocket fuel for the rupee and the inflation outlook — but the truce is far from sealed.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; India's benchmarks logged their longest winning run in two months as oil eased
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs, this rally is a three-way win and a warning at once — cheaper oil eases India's import bill and supports the rupee that governs every remittance, while the fragility of the Iran truce means the gains rest on a deal that could still unravel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Fear Gutted India's IT Stocks by 27%. Now Some of the World's Biggest Investors Are Calling It a Bargain.
articles.excerpt: The Nifty IT index has been hammered as investors bet that artificial intelligence will hollow out India's software outsourcing giants. But with BlackRock and others arguing the market has been 'over-punished,' the very sector everyone is fleeing is starting to look like the contrarian call of 2026.
articles.image_caption: A Tata Consultancy Services building; India's IT index has fallen about 27% in 2026 on AI-disruption fears
articles.nri_angle: India's IT giants are the bedrock of countless NRI portfolios and the employers of a generation of diaspora engineers — so the question of whether AI is a death sentence or an overblown panic for TCS, Infosys and Wipro is both a financial and a deeply personal one for Indian software professionals abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After a Record $30 Billion Exodus, Foreign Money Is Edging Back Into India. The Tide May Be Turning.
articles.excerpt: Foreign investors yanked a record $30.8 billion out of Indian equities in 2026 — then turned net buyers for the first time in 13 sessions as a US-Iran peace deal cooled oil and the RBI moved to steady the rupee. Wall Street firms now say India was 'over-punished,' and its absence from the AI trade may finally be an advantage.
articles.image_caption: A stock market display; foreign investors edged back into Indian equities this week
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who watched Indian equities and their rupee-denominated portfolios slide through a brutal first half of 2026, the early signs of a foreign-money reversal reframe the question from 'how much more will I lose?' to whether the worst is now behind — and whether the diaspora's home-country bias is, for once, the contrarian call.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
